mode: Native PostgreSQL persistent view removal with UTF-8 identifiers, standard-conforming strings, case-sensitive names and explicit schemas.

DropView.role: A complete removal of one or more persistent views of one explicitly specified kind.
DropView.structure: One view kind, an ordered nonempty owned list of absolute names, an absence policy, a dependency policy and the native release.
DropView.conditions: Accept distinct checked view identities. Resolve known targets to the requested kind in analysis. A known absence with IF EXISTS requires an explicit known schema and a complete catalog.
DropView.meaning: Delete exact ordinary or materialized views. RESTRICT rejects an unlisted dependent object. CASCADE removes the transitive dependent closure. The operation is transactional.
DropView.sql: Print DROP and the exact view kind, the optional existence clause, ordered qualified names and an explicit dependency policy.

ViewName.role: The exact persistent catalog identity of a view removal target.
ViewName.structure: One decoded schema identifier and one decoded view identifier.
ViewName.conditions: Both identifiers obey the existing PostgreSQL identifier domain. A temporary namespace is outside this persistent role.
ViewName.meaning: Identify this single catalog coordinate within the selected database and profile.
ViewName.sql: Quote both identifier components in schema and view order.

ViewRemovalKind.role: The native kind required of every target in a view removal.
ViewRemovalKind.conditions: The same single closed kind applies to each target.
ViewRemovalKind.meaning: Select the native object-kind checks and removal rules for the named view population.
ViewRemovalKind.sql: Write the exact VIEW or MATERIALIZED VIEW clause.

structure: Separate the catalog kind, absence behavior, dependency behavior and absolute ordered target identities.
conditions: Support ordinary and materialized persistent views with names resolved in the same database and language profile. Reject missing required identities, wrong kinds, unknown schema absence and repeat targets at construction.
meaning: Remove the named views and, only under CASCADE, their dependent views. An error aborts the current transaction. IF EXISTS tolerates a known absence. Native rollback restores changed catalog contents.
sql: Emit the selected view kind, existence policy, fully qualified distinct targets and CASCADE or RESTRICT from the immutable value.

Transaction activity, in-transaction marker and post-rollback restoration

finite.completeness: Recover each clause and ordered target selection from the loaded graph and verify fixture dependencies independently before each statement. Exhaust the full Cartesian product on each pin.

evidence.P01: Record the exact target identities, kind, clause policies and native profile.
evidence.P02: Check role, distinction, scope and known-name resolution before publication.
evidence.P03: Retain only immutable semantic identities and clause choices.
evidence.P04: Combine kind, absence, dependency and the exact target sequence under native DDL rules.
evidence.P05: Own the detached targets and use final immutable identifiers and a closed enum.
evidence.P06: Render the operation from the exact structured value.
evidence.Q01: Check the fixed independent invalid constructions and guarded code shapes.
evidence.Q02: Accept all required finite direct and analyzed inputs for each release.
evidence.Q03: Compare independent predictions for catalog deletion, dependency closure and transaction rollback.
evidence.Q04: Compare native observations from both authored and emitted SQL.
evidence.Q05: Link production construction and rendering to the two installed package layouts and exact artifacts.

open: Authorization and owner failures depend on the executing session.
The native test fixtures use ordinary and materialized view dependency chains with stable object contents. They do not exhaust PostgreSQL catalog dependency graph kinds.
The PDO observer records success and error SQLSTATE. Informational notices, including the textual reports of CASCADE or a skipped absence, are outside the effect observation in this domain.
